title: A Field Deployment at MBARI
summary: A July 2024 field deployment brought me to MBARI in Moss Landing, where I learned to tie knots and ended up at the Monterey Bay Aquarium.
coverAlt: A MINION float mounted on a yellow frame on the deck of a boat

body.text: In July 2024, I went to the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) for a field deployment. It was my first time working with so many oceanographers at once. I quickly realized how much I still had to learn, and I got a little flustered. Melissa spent quite a while teaching me how to tie knots. I was grateful she took the time.

body.alt: A MINION float mounted on a yellow frame on the deck of a boat
body.caption: A MINION float on deck during the deployment trip.

body.text: MBARI struck me as a wonderful place to work. One thing that stuck with me was the indoor seawater test tank, which is 10 meters deep. I can imagine how much fun it would be to have a tank like that on hand when building an ocean instrument.

body.alt: An indoor seawater test tank with yellow railings along one side
body.caption: MBARI’s 10-meter-deep seawater test tank.

body.alt: A MINION float suspended underwater in front of the tank’s viewing windows
body.caption: A MINION float seen through a window in the test tank.

body.alt: A penguin cartoon, a quote about computers, and a bioluminescence sticker
body.caption: A few things that caught my eye at MBARI.

body.text: MBARI is in Moss Landing, which felt like a peculiar little corner of sunny California. It seemed to be overcast almost the whole time I was there. I’ll leave you to look up why.

About half an hour away in Monterey is the Monterey Bay Aquarium, which I loved. I was really into Dave the Diver at the time, and I came away with a hunch that its developers must be regulars there. I also loved this sea otter bag.

body.alt: A canvas shoulder bag illustrated with floating sea otters
body.caption: The sea otter bag I couldn’t stop looking at.
